title: Lazar's 'gravity wave A' may be a garbled QCD theta term / Chern-Simons

tellings.quote: Is it possible, Eric, that what he's talking about is that the theta term from QCD is what he's calling stupidly gravity wave A, which no person I've ever heard of has ever used that terminology.

plain: Bob Lazar, a man who says he worked on alien craft at a secret site called S4 near Area 51 in 1989, spoke of a force he called "gravity wave A", and the mathematician Eric Weinstein wonders if this was a garbled version of a real idea in physics: the "theta term" in the theory of the strong nuclear force, or a related structure called Chern-Simons. Weinstein raises it on the show, noting that no one he knows of has ever used Lazar's phrase. If so, Lazar may have heard real physics and repeated it badly.
